cases.excerpt: During a median follow-up of 28.3 years, we documented 6,980 incident prostate cancer cases including 1,053 lethal and 1,143 aggressive.

effect_size.excerpt: However, compared to never-users, men who used supplement zinc more than 75 mg/day were at higher risk for lethal (HR: 1.76, 95% CI: 1.16-2.66, P<sub>trend</sub> = 0.001) and aggressive prostate cancer (HR: 1.80, 95% CI: 1.19-2.73, P<sub>trend</sub> = 0.006). headline.funnel_interpretation: Egger’s test is generally not recommended when fewer than 10 studies are available.
headline.results_interpretation: The pooled analysis of 2 studies yielded an effect size of 0.84 (95% CI: 0.17–4.29), indicating no statistically significant association between zinc and aggressive prostate cancer. Although the point estimate suggests a potential inverse relationship, the confidence interval includes the null. These findings were accompanied by very high heterogeneity (I² = 87.79%), reflecting highly inconsistent results across studies.
